page: Amazon Web Services t9g.medium is an entry-level burstable instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and custom AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 silicon. Operating at a fixed clock speed of 3.3 GHz, the instance provisions 2 physical cores and 2 vCPUs with 1 thread per core, accompanied by 4.0 GB of system memory (2.0 GB per core). The underlying CPU cache architecture provides 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache. It lacks dedicated hardware GPUs and includes no local instance storage, requiring remote EBS block storage volumes. Baseline network throughput is rated at 0 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluation reveals strong single-threaded CPU capability, highlighted by a Geekbench single-core score of 2293.0 and top-tier single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 16.83 GB/sec, alongside strong gzip compression throughput. In contrast, aggregate multi-core throughput remains modest due to the 2-vCPU cap, resulting in bottom-quartile scores in multi-core stress-ng tests and Clang software compilation. Memory performance shows solid large-block read bandwidth of 65.17 GB/sec, while large-block write operations register lower at 25.63 GB/sec. Redis SET benchmarks achieved 6.6 million operations per second, with static web serving throughput reaching 9.26 GB/sec.

From an efficiency standpoint, the t9g.medium provides an economical footprint for workloads that exhibit intermittent resource demands. The burstable CPU allocation model allows users to pay for low sustained resource consumption while tapping into top-tier single-thread burst performance. However, workloads requiring continuous multi-core execution or sustained network data transfer will encounter the constraints of the CPU credit allocation and lack of baseline network bandwidth.

The t9g.medium is best aligned with lightweight applications, low-traffic web serving, development environments, microservices, and background asynchronous jobs that benefit from modern ARM64 single-core performance without requiring dedicated full-core execution.
description: Amazon Web Services t9g.medium is a burstable ARM64 general-purpose instance powered by AWS Nitro and a 3.3 GHz ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 processor. The system configuration includes 2 vCPUs across 2 physical cores, 4.0 GB of RAM, no local instance storage, and no GPU accelerators. Baseline network bandwidth is configured at 0 Gbps. Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier single-core performance, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 2293.0 and high-speed data decompression, contrasted by lower multi-threaded throughput typical of a two-core footprint. Memory bandwidth remains solid for large reads, and the server achieves 6.6 million Redis operations per second. With burstable CPU credits and an efficient resource allocation profile, the t9g.medium is well matched for lightweight microservices, testing environments, low-traffic web servers, and intermittent computing workloads.
